intended_object: The canonical quotient map sending a short augmented form g to its class in the short augmented misère monoid, i.e. short augmented forms taken modulo misère equivalence relative to the universe of short forms. Inferred from the docstring and the definition of `ShortQuotient` just above it.
explanation: `ShortQuotient` is defined as `MisereQuotient (G := AugmentedForm) IsShort`. That is the quotient of the subtype `{g // IsShort g}` by the setoid "g =m h modulo IsShort", i.e. misère equivalence relative to the short forms. `MisereQuotient.mk` is `Quotient.mk` for this setoid. `mkShort g hg` is just `mk ⟨g, hg⟩`: it packages the form and its shortness proof into the subtype and takes its class. So it is exactly the class map into the short augmented misère quotient, and the library uses it that way: it is additive, sends 0 to 0, and the classes of normal forms are units. The definition is specific to short augmented forms on purpose, because the quotient it maps into is that specific monoid, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no counterpart: it has no misère game theory.
